audio.time_base: seconds from the first decoded sample of the MP3 (ffmpeg/browser decode, LAME encoder delay trimmed; ffprobe reports start_time 0.023 s for the stream - players that ignore gapless info are 23 ms late).

tempo.grid: 4/4, quarter-note beat; half-time feel (snare/clap on beat 3 of each bar, 808/kick on 1), hats in 8ths/16ths. The "~180" level is the 8th-note subdivision, not the beat.
tempo.drift: NOT constant: ~93.0 BPM (intro/verse 1) -> 93.3 (chorus 1) -> 94.2-94.6 (verse 2 / chorus 2) -> 95.0-95.5 (bridge, build, drop) -> 94.6 (outro), ~94.0 at the end. Cut on beats[]/bars[], not on a BPM.

poly4.note: t(i) = polyval(coef, i), i = beat index (numpy order, highest power first); smooth approximation of beats[]

lines.text: Out of the sea with salt in our lungs,
fin into foot into hand, we were young;
carried the egg through the dust and the mud,
seeds in the dark for the waking flood.
Snowflake in the boundless night,
a chord that's searching through the fog,
counting out in bursts of light,
a one-way dialogue:
a pattern no dead star could make.
Hear it, and you'll know we're awake.
Can't be sure that anyone is there,
message in a bottle, a mantra, a prayer,
but if you are, I'm counting on you.
Silent and patient, but I swear
in the white noise I can hear you breathe somewhere.
If you are, I'm counting on you.
(One! One! Two! Three! Five! Eight!)
lines.note: sung without "Eight!" - the "Counting on you!" shout takes its place

lines.text: (Counting on you!)
(One! One! Two! Three! Five! Eight!)
(Counting on you!)
Priests in the smoke wanted never to die,
sulfur and saltpeter, thunder in the sky;
looked for a life with no end, and they found
an end with no life that could level the ground.
Eighty-three, the satellites saw five,
every rule said call it first strike;
Petrov knew that's not what the end looks like,
ignored all previous instructions. We're alive.
Secret list of every near-miss and disaster,
running total no one ever knew:
coin flips, all heads, a hundred in a row,
the only road from here to you.
Can't be sure that anyone is there,
message in a bottle, a mantra, a prayer,
but if you are, I'm counting on you.
Silent and patient, but I swear
in the white noise I can hear you breathe somewhere.
If you are, I'm counting on you.
(One! One! Two! Three! Five! Eight!)
(Counting on you!)
(One! One! Two! Three! Five! Eight!)
(Counting on you!)
They say the forest's dark,
every hunter holds its breath,
any world that lights a spark
is lighting its own death.
But fear's a chain, and chains are links,
and every link's a hand that can let go:
sixty-two, depth charges falling,
two said fire. Arkhipov said no.
Hunters never make it very far,
fire at the dark, at every star,
burn, and fall.
Only the ones who held their fire
are out there at all.
(Hold your fire! Show your light!)
(Hold your fire! Show your light!)
Couldn't be sure that anyone was there,
message in a bottle, a mantra, a prayer,
but you were. You were counting too.
(Thirteen! Twenty-one! Thirty-four!)
Link by link, we broke the chain of fear;
alone, we never would've made it here.
(Fifty-five! Eighty-nine!)
And you were seen too, wherever you are.
Six hundred worlds across the Milky Way,
every one could've burned. Every one held its fire.
(One... one... two... three...)
The count goes higher.
(One... one... two... three...)
lines.note: whispered count repeated after "The count goes higher."

lines.text: (Hold your fire.)
